Check Ollama speed in the terminal

Replace LOCAL_MODEL with a tag from ollama list. After the reply, look for eval rate for generation and prompt eval rate for prompt processing.

ollama run LOCAL_MODEL --verbose "Reply with exactly LOCAL_OK and nothing else."

Download the measured CLI timings. This check used a three-token reply. Use a fixed prompt and a longer output for comparisons.

Record an Ollama benchmark request with curl

Run ollama list to find your local model tag. Change qwen2.5:0.5b and the port in this example to match your server. The request keeps the model loaded for the repeat check. Use a scratch model if other apps depend on your running service.

curl --noproxy '*' -fsS --max-time 60 \
  http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model":"qwen2.5:0.5b",
    "prompt":"Explain why the Moon stays in orbit in six short numbered points.",
    "stream":false,
    "keep_alive":"5m",
    "options":{"num_ctx":2048,"num_predict":64,"temperature":0}
  }'

Paste the complete JSON into the calculator. Use "stream":true to get NDJSON and add -N to curl to see partial lines. A client that wants to measure first visible text must time that event as it receives the stream.

What do you want to explain?

Check the waitCompare ratesFind the fields

Explain a long wait before the first text

Start with load_duration and prompt_eval_duration. Model loading and input processing can take time before text appears. Check ollama ps before the request to see whether the model is already loaded. Keep the same model, context and prompt when repeating the request. Record whether the prompt repeats because cache reuse can change the reported timings.

Ollama returns server durations in nanoseconds. Total server duration covers the reported request, including generation. To measure time to first text, use a monotonic client timer from request start to the first non-empty response text. The final JSON alone cannot recover that time.

Compare generation with prompt processing speed

  • Generation rate. Divide eval_count by eval_duration ÷ 1,000,000,000.
  • Prompt processing rate. Subtract prompt_eval_cached_count from prompt_eval_count, then divide by prompt_eval_duration ÷ 1,000,000,000. If the cache count is missing, the calculator uses the reported token count and labels that result.

Compare several runs with the same quantization, context, output budget, concurrency and prompt. Keep the first run separate from the resident runs. If the generation phase stays slow, check CPU and GPU placement in ollama ps. If first output is slow while generation is fast, compare model loading and the input phase before changing GPU settings.

Recover timing fields when they are missing

Use one completed native response. The /v1/chat/completions route can report token usage through the OpenAI-compatible schema. Its usage counts alone do not give the native generation and prompt durations. If an NDJSON capture stops before "done": true, retry and keep the final record.

A missing count or duration leaves that rate unavailable. A zero duration also leaves the rate unavailable. done_reason: "length" is a completed timing record when generation stops at its token limit. A finished load-only or unload request provides no generation measurement.

See the official Generate API and Chat API, or the native NDJSON and compatible SSE examples. The cache subtraction follows the Ollama 0.40.18 CLI timing calculation.

What changed when the model stayed loaded

On one Apple M4 with 32 GiB, we sent one request with the model absent from /api/ps and three identical requests after it was loaded. Tests used Ollama 0.40.18 and the same Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M GGUF. Each request generated 64 tokens. Operating system caches were not cleared.

  • First request. Server reported 0.5570 s loading and 146.71 tokens/s in generation. First text arrived after 0.6012 s.
  • Three resident requests. Server reported 162.42–165.26 tokens/s in generation. First text arrived after 0.0076–0.0079 s. Each repeat reported 42 cached tokens out of 43. The test did not isolate the separate effects of residency and cache reuse.

Download the per-request timings, paste the measured JSON response or paste the complete NDJSON capture. These short runs reflect one model and a repeated prompt on one machine. For another engine and larger models, see the Mac mini M4 Qwen benchmark.
